title: Startup of the Reverse Host
statement: Let $S$ and $V$ be deterministic Turing machines over the binary alphabet, let $x$ be a binary word, and let $w$ be a binary word of length $2|x|+2$. Running the reverse host on the choices in $w$ from its initial configuration on $x$ yields the guessing-phase configuration for the input-normalized scheduler's initial configuration on $x$, with empty guessed word.
hypotheses_covered: $S,V$ are finite deterministic machines over the binary alphabet
$w$ is a binary word with length $2|x|+2$
replaced: Let $S, V$ be deterministic machines, $x$ an input, and $w$ any word of choice bits with $|w| = 2|x| + 2$. Running the reverse host under $w$ from its blank-tape initial configuration on $x$ reaches the guessing-phase configuration for the initial configuration of the input-normalized scheduler on $x$ with empty guessed word; all startup choices are ignored.
